newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - August 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - August 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Bangladesh has withdrawn reservations about some provisions of the Convention on Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women relating to personal rights such as family benefits and guardianship of children.
The road communication between Chittagong and Cox's Bazar town was cut off on Saturday as the highway went under flood waters at many points.
Private sector is expected to share 58 percent of the development outlay in Bangladesh's fifth five year plan (1997-2002)
The Sundarbans mangrove forest of Bangladesh is likely to be declared by the UNESCO as a Natural Heritage Site.
Some five hundred million people are exposed to the threats of arsenic contamination in Bangladesh which tops the countries with arsenic problems, followed by India and China, says a study.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has called strike in northeast Sylhet district on August 5 to press for restoration of Dhaka-Sylhet rail communications that snapped following a gas field fire on June 15.
Bangladesh Garments Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) said it would soon arrange insurance coverage for 1.3 million garment workers.
At least 160,000 people die of cancer every year in Bangladesh REUTER
